%   This distribution may include materials developed by third parties.
%
%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%

\section{Aggregate Expressions}
\seclabel{aggregate-expr}

\note{Some operators and matrix unpasting are not yet supported.}

\note{\EXP{\mapsto} is a special syntax only in two contexts:
map aggregates and map comprehensions. (02/12/09)
}
\emph{RectSeparator} &::=& \EXP{;}+\\
&$|$& \emph{Whitespace}\\

\emph{MapExpr} &::=& \{ \option{\emph{StaticArgs}} \option{\emph{EntryList}} \}\\
\end{Grammar}

\emph{Aggregate expressions} evaluate to values that are themselves
homogeneous collections of values.  Each subexpression of an aggregate
expression is evaluated in parallel in a separate implicit thread (see
\secref{threads-parallelism}).
With the exception of array expressions, the resulting
values are passed to the appropriate bracketing operator, which is a
function with a varargs parameter constructing the aggregate.
The array aggregate operations
construct the aggregate directly, after all
subexpressions have completed normally.  Any aggregate expression may
reserve storage for its result before its elements complete
evaluation.

Functions defining aggregate expressions are provided in \library\
for sets, maps, lists, matrices, vectors, and arrays.

\subsection{Set Expressions}
\seclabel{set-expr}

Set element expressions are enclosed in braces and separated by commas.
The type of a set expression is
\EXP{\TYP{Set}\llbracket T\rrbracket},
where \VAR{T} is the union type
of the types of all element expressions of the set expression.


Set containment is checked with the operator $\in$
and the subset relationship is checked with the operator \EXP{\subseteq}.
For example:
\input{\home/basic/examples/Expr.Set.tex}
evaluates to \VAR{true}.
and
\marginnote{This example should be added to the SpecData directory when it works.}
\begin{center}
\EXP{\{0, 1, 2\} \subseteq \{0, 3, 2\}}
\end{center}
evaluates to \VAR{false}.

\seclabel{array-expr}

Array element expressions are enclosed in brackets. Element expressions
along a row are separated only by whitespace.
Two dimensional array expressions are written by separating rows with
newlines or semicolons.  If a semicolon appears, whitespace before
and after the semicolon is ignored.
The parts of higher-dimensional array expressions are separated
by repeated-semicolons, where the dimensionality
of the result is equal to one plus the number
of repeated semicolons.
The type of a $k$-dimensional array expression is
\EXP{\TYP{Array}k\llbracket{}T, 0, n_{\mathrm{0}}, \cdots,
         0, n_{k-1}\rrbracket},
where \VAR{T} is the union type of the types of the element expressions and
$n_0, ..., n_{k-1}$
are the sizes of the array in each dimension\footnote{
As of March 2008, the Fortress library provides \EXP{\TYP{Array}k} types for
$1 \le k \le 3$.}. This type can be abbreviated as
\EXP{T [n_{\mathrm{0}}, \cdots, n_{k-1}]}.

content.content:
We call the source code for a single software component a \emph{project}.
Typically, when a project written in other programming languages is compiled,
each file in the project is separately compiled.
To ship an application,
these files are linked together to form an application or library.
Fortress uses a different model:
a project is compiled directly into a single component,
which is installed in the compiling fortress.

From the point of view of the compiler, all the source code for a
project is contained in a single file.  This approach simplifies the design
but it is unworkable for
components of substantial size.  Therefore, the compiler can be
instructed to concatenate several source files together before
compiling, while maintaining the original source location
information.

After these components are compiled from source files, they can then
be linked together to form larger components.





\section{Components}
\seclabel{components}

#!/bin/bash
# Rung C: parse Library/FortressLibrary.fss and .fsi as they are at <base-commit> and as they are in
# the working tree, with the tree's own parser (bin/fortress parse -out), and compare the two parse
# trees with every source position mapped back to the base numbering (ast-compare.py); see REPORT.md.
# usage, from $FORTRESS_HOME after ant compileAll: parse-compare.sh <base-commit> <scratch-dir>
set -u
BASE=$1 ; S=$2
D=$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)
mkdir -p "$S/base/Library"
for f in fss fsi ; do
    git show "$BASE:Library/FortressLibrary.$f" > "$S/base/Library/FortressLibrary.$f"
    ( cd "$S/base" && "$FORTRESS_HOME/bin/fortress" parse -out "$S/pre-$f.tfs" "Library/FortressLibrary.$f" ) | head -1 | sed "s/^/base $f: /"
    "$FORTRESS_HOME/bin/fortress" parse -out "$S/post-$f.tfs" "Library/FortressLibrary.$f" | head -1 | sed "s/^/tree $f: /"
    python3 "$D/ast-compare.py" "$BASE" "Library/FortressLibrary.$f" "$S/pre-$f.tfs" "$S/post-$f.tfs"
done
EOF
chmod +x $R/parse-compare.sh $R/*.py && git rm -q $R/ast-digest.py $R/probes/ast-digest-preedit.txt && ls $R $R/probes

# Rung C of climb batch 3: four comments in the interpreter library

- problem: explorations/coordinator/POSITIONS.md:47 (the closure's `NOT YET` comment, asked for "either way") and :44 (the `Array3` clause and the scalar block approved as landed, on the explainer's defaults for them at explorations/coordinator/postmortem-2026-09-19/library-findings-explained.md:193, :249-255, :272-283)
- spec: Specification/basic/traits.tex:76-88 (`extends` takes `TraitTypeWhere`, `comprises` only `TraitTypes`) and :231-236 (the comprises list is exactly the immediate subtraits); Specification/basic/traits.tex:218-222 with Specification/advanced/overloading.tex:178-216 for the `Array3` exclusion; none for the scalar block (no prose on array-scalar arithmetic or rank-3 algebra: `grep -rn -i 'scalar\|elementwise\|element-wise' Specification/basic Specification/basic-lib` has no hit on arrays)
- precedent: Library/FortressLibrary.fss:1297, :1374, :1589-1590 (the `.fss` `NOT YET` form) and Library/FortressLibrary.fsi:818, :1063 (the `.fsi` `not yet:` form); Library/FortressLibrary.fss:4503 (the scalar block's own `(*)` header comment)
- deviation: the closure note sits on the line after the one-line trait, not inside a trait body as at .fss:1297, since putting it inside would change a code line (Library/FortressLibrary.fss:613); the `.fsi` note uses the `.fsi`'s own `not yet:` form, not the `.fss` form the brief quotes (Library/FortressLibrary.fsi:410); the honest clause is spelled without braces, `comprises Integral[\I\] where [\I\]`, as the team spells its single-type notes (Library/FortressLibrary.fss:1297), where the brief writes `comprises { Integral[\I\] where [\I\] }`; the example is written in Fortress's array syntax `3 - [1 2]` (Specification/basic/expressions/aggregate.tex:120-121) where the brief writes `[1, 2]` (Library/FortressLibrary.fss:4512); the reversed `-` is at base .fss:4500, not :4501 as the brief and the explainer cite, and the note sits beside it by symbol (Library/FortressLibrary.fss:4512-4515); the `.fsi` block, which had no header, gets the `.fss` block's header line as well (Library/FortressLibrary.fsi:2547)
- historical: Library/FortressLibrary.fss, Library/FortressLibrary.fsi

Line numbers of the two library files are this branch's, after the edit, unless marked
"base" (the tree at `d610695c0`). The base-to-branch shift is in section 8.

## 1. What changed

Comment text only: 31 lines inserted, none deleted, no other file of the original tree touched.

```
$ git diff --stat d610695c0c014001687e528fa9fd99078db6ea76 -- Library/
 Library/FortressLibrary.fsi | 16 ++++++++++++++++
 Library/FortressLibrary.fss | 15 +++++++++++++++
 2 files changed, 31 insertions(+)
```

1. **The closure** (`trait AnyIntegral extends { QQ } comprises { ZZ } end`, .fss:612, .fsi:409).
   The line after it, in each file's own form:
   - .fss:613 `(** \vspace{-4ex} NOT YET: %comprises Integral[\I\] where [\I\]% *)`
   - .fsi:410 `(** not yet: ``%comprises Integral[\I\] where [\I\]%'' *)`
2. **Why `Array3` excludes `AnyAdditiveGroup`** (.fss:2671-2676 under the clause at :2670;
   .fsi:1661-1666 under :1660), the same six lines in both files:
   ```
   (* Excluding AnyAdditiveGroup picks one of two uses of rank 3.  An operator
      between an Array3 and a number or a lower-rank array, such as a matrix added
      to every plane, can be declared without colliding with AdditiveGroup's
      +(self, other: T); in exchange no Array3 can be an additive group, a rank-3
      counterpart of Vector and Matrix.  Array1 and Array2 cannot exclude it:
      Vector and Matrix extend them and are additive groups. *)
   ```
3. **The unsized result** (.fss:4504-4508 under the block's header at :4503; .fsi:2547-2552,
   header included):
   ```
   (*) All eight return the unsized Array[\T,I\], where the Vector and Matrix scalar
   (*) operators keep rank and size (Vector[\T,n\] to Vector[\T,n\]).  Nothing is lost at run
   (*) time, since map builds its result with replica and m + 1.0 is still a Matrix; a static
   (*) checker sees only Array[\T,I\], so sized arrays under a compiler need per-shape
   (*) declarations beside these.
   ```
4. **What the reversed `-` means** (.fss:4512-4514 above it at :4515; .fsi:2556-2558 above :2559):
   ```
   (*) Scalar on the left: y - x is y - e for each element e of x, so 3 - [1 2] is [2 1].
   (*) This is the only pair here whose two orders differ: +, MIN and MAX commute, and so do
   (*) the scalar DOT and juxtaposition pairs of Vector and Matrix that this block follows.
   ```

No declaration, clause, body or name changed; no clause moved. Nothing here needed a word of
Fortress changed, so the rung's stop condition did not arise.

## 2. Where the fix belongs

The feature is the comment (`map/spec-to-implementation.md:168`: `basic/lexical-structure.tex:700`,
`Spacing.rats`, works on both paths, ledger row 217). A comment is whitespace to the lexer
(`Specification/basic/lexical-structure.tex:704-719` and :730-760; the grammar at
`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/parser/Spacing.rats:24-90`), so the site is simply the two
library files at the four declarations, and the only way a comment can change the program is by
its delimiters: `(*` inside a comment opens a nested one, `*)` closes it, and `(*)` is a comment to
the end of the line (`Spacing.rats:46-88`; row 217 is the trap). The four texts contain no `(*`
and no `*)` except as their own delimiters, which `comment-only-check.py` checks mechanically
(section 5). The compiler's prelude (`CompilerLibrary`, `CompilerBuiltin`) does not import
`FortressLibrary`, so the compiled path and the ladder cannot see these lines; the checker-count
stage is the one compile-path consumer of these two files.

## 3. Precedent search

- **The `NOT YET` note.** The `.fss` has it three times, all in one form:
  `(** \vspace{-4ex} NOT YET: %comprises … where …% *)` at .fss:1297 (`AnyMaybe`), :1374
  (`AnyUniqueItem`) and :1589-1590 (`HasRank`, with a bound: `where [\T,E,I\]{ T extends
  Array[\T,E,I\] }`), each on the line after the trait header, inside the body. The `.fsi` mirrors
  two of the three in a different form, `(** not yet: ``%comprises … where …%'' *)`, at .fsi:818
  (`AnyMaybe`) and :1063 (`HasRank`); its `AnyUniqueItem` (.fsi:886-889) carries none. So two
  forms exist, one per file, and I followed each file's own. The `\vspace{-4ex}` pulls the note up
  against the rendered line above it (the `(**` comments are the doc comments the Fortify tools
  typeset, `Fortify/fortify-doc.txt:360-378`), which is why the note goes after the one-line
  trait rather than before it.
- **The spelling of the clause.** The two unbounded precedents write a single type without braces
  (`comprises Maybe[\T\] where [\T\]`); the bounded one spells its bound. `Integral`'s parameter is
  bounded (`I extends Integral[\I\]`), but the approved text, the explainer
  (`library-findings-explained.md:64-65`) and the trace (`perf-probes/prelude/exclusion-trace.md:297-298`)
  all write `where [\I\]`, so I kept that and dropped only the braces.
- **Rationale for an exclusion, in a comment.** The library writes it as a plain `(* … *)` comment:
  the Potemkin note (.fss:1600-1601) and the `AnyMaybe` note (.fss:1294-1295, "This makes excludes
  work without where clauses"). The `Array3` comment follows that form, placed directly under the
  clause it explains.
- **The scalar block.** Its own header (.fss:4503) is a `(*)` line comment, and the `.fsi`'s nearby
  header (.fsi:2543) is too; items 3 and 4 use the same form.

## 4. The specification, comment by comment

1. **The closure.** `Specification/basic/traits.tex:231-236` (a note box): the traits listed in a
   `comprises` clause "are exactly the traits that immediately extend" the trait, so
   `comprises { ZZ }` is false while `Integral[\I\]` (.fss:615) extends `AnyIntegral` directly. The
   true statement names every instantiation of `Integral`, and the grammar has no way to say so:
   `extends` takes `TraitTypeWheres`, a type with an optional `where` (`traits.tex:76-83`), but
   `comprises` takes only `TraitTypes` (`:88`), and the parser matches
   (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/parser/NoNewlineHeader.rats:96-135`). That is what the
   team's `NOT YET` says; the note says it and nothing more, and promises no checker change.
2. **`Array3`.** An `excludes` clause means no trait can extend both (`traits.tex:218-222`); two
   types that exclude have subtypes that exclude (`types-vals-vars.tex:163-164`); tuple types
   exclude if a pair of their elements do (`:276-277`); and "without coercion, incompatibility is
   equivalent to exclusion" (`Specification/advanced/overloading.tex:182`), which makes two
   declarations with incompatible parameter types a valid overloading (`:212-216`). So an operator
   one of whose parameters is an `Array3` never overlaps `AdditiveGroup[\T\]`'s `+(self, other: T)`
   (.fss:334), whatever `T` is, because `T` extends `AnyAdditiveGroup`. The price is the clause's
   plain meaning: no type extends both `Array3` and `AdditiveGroup`. `Array1` and `Array2` cannot
   carry the same exclusion because `Vector` (.fss:2193-2194) and `Matrix` extend them and are
   additive groups, and `traits.tex:222` forbids extending two excluding traits. On which future
   rank 3 should have, the specification is silent: its prose makes a one- and two-dimensional
   numeric array a vector and a matrix (`Specification/basic/expressions/aggregate.tex:150-166`)
   and says nothing of rank 3 beyond indexing. The choice is Pavol's, taken 2026-09-21.
   The "future one" use is already gated: `ProjectFortress/test_library/ArrayOperatorVocabulary.fsi:6-7`
   declares the plane-wise `+` between a `Matrix` and an `Array3`, and
   `ProjectFortress/tests/ArrayOperatorsBesideLibrary.fss:22-23` checks it (run singly after the
   edit: `probes/gated-tests-postedit.txt`). That is the interpreter, which does not check a user
   declaration's overloading against the library's; the checker's view of it was not measured.
3. **The unsized result, and 4. the reversed `-`.** The specification's prose has no array-scalar
   arithmetic at all (the grep in the provenance block), so both are library decisions, taken on
   2026-09-21 as the explainer's defaults 3a-A and 3b-A. What the comments state as fact was
   measured under `walk` (`probes/CommentedDecls.fss`, capture `probes/CommentedDecls-postedit.txt`):
   `3 - x` is `[0#2][ 2 1 ]` for `x: ZZ32[2] = [1 2]` and `x - 3` is `[0#2][ -2 -1 ]`; `m + 1.0`
   and `0.0 MAX m` are `Matrix[\RR64,2,2\]` at run time, `1.0 - v` a `Vector[\RR64,3\]`, and
   `10.0 - t` an `Array3` (the `replica` claim, .fss:2139-2140, :2401-2402, :2770-2772). The gated
   `ProjectFortress/tests/ArrayScalarExtension.fss:23` and `:45` already pin the reversed `-`
   (`(1.0 - v)[0] = 2.0`, `(1 - iv)[0] = 2`). The precedents' commutativity: every Vector and Matrix
   scalar pair calls the same `me.scale(other)` in both orders (.fss:2266-2281, :2648-2658).

## 5. How the change was verified

A comment-only rung has nothing to make red, as the batch record says, so there is no failing test
and no `.test` file. What stands in for the recorded failure is the base tree's own behaviour,
captured before the edit existed (commit `76c55b270`), and the same captures after it:

- **The diff is comment-only**, checked mechanically: `comment-only-check.py` re-lexes both files
  with the comment rules of `Spacing.rats` and reports 0 deleted lines, 0 added lines that are not
  wholly comment, and token streams without comments identical before and after, for both files
  (`probes/comment-only-check.txt`, section (d)). The same capture shows the check failing on three
  deliberate mutations: a code line added (a), a `(*)` turned into an unbalanced `(*` (b), one word
  of code changed (c).
- **The parser builds the same trees.** `parse-compare.sh` parses both files as they are at the base
  commit and as they are now, with the tree's own parser (`bin/fortress parse -out`), maps every
  source position of the new trees back to the base numbering, and compares (`ast-compare.py`;
  capture `probes/parse-compare.txt`). Of 29,058 spans and 1,355 location-derived names in the
  `.fss` and 12,399 and 1,008 in the `.fsi`, all agree except three declarations whose span end
  moved onto the comment that now follows them: the `.fss`'s first `-` of the scalar block and the
  `.fsi`'s `SUFFIX_SUM` and first `-` (six dump lines). That is a property of the parser, measured
  in section 6, D1; nothing else in either tree differs. The comparator catches a one-word code
  change as "anything else" (`probes/parse-compare-mutation.txt`).
- **The checker sees the same library.** The gate's count stage
  (`explorations/coordinator/tools/checker-count/run.sh`), run before and after:
  `probes/checker-count-preedit.txt` and `-postedit.txt` are identical (93 errors, 52 locations, the
  same per-api rows, the same `NativeArray` crash line, `#shadow` matching). The checker's full
  output (`probes/checker-count-preedit-run.txt`, `-postedit-run.txt`) differs in 96 raw lines, all
  line numbers, and is identical, 253 lines in the same order, once `remap-lines.py` maps the new
  positions back (`probes/post-edit-comparisons.txt`). This rung declares no `expectedCheckerCount`
  and moves none.
- **The interpreter runs the same.** `probes/CommentedDecls.fss` exercises all four commented
  declarations; its output is identical before and after (`probes/CommentedDecls-preedit.txt`,
  `-postedit.txt`). Four gated interpreter tests that use them, run singly after the edit
  (`ArrayScalarExtension`, `ArrayOperatorsBesideLibrary`, `ReplicaTest`, `array3test`), all exit 0
  with their expected output (`probes/gated-tests-postedit.txt`).
- **The two suites were not run here** (decision 1 in section 9). What they will show at the gate
  follows from the above: every interpreter test sees a parse tree equal to the base's up to
  positions, so no pass or fail can move, and the counts and both summaries stay as they are. What
  can change in the logs is text that prints a `FortressLibrary` position: every position below an
  insertion shifts, and a dispatch failure that lists the scalar block's first `-` now prints its
  span as ending in the comment (`probes/ArrayLiteralArg-postedit.txt` against
  `probes/ArrayLiteralArg.txt`: 26 raw lines differ, one after remapping). No `.test` expectation
  in any corpus contains a `FortressLibrary` position (`grep -rn 'FortressLibrary' --include=*.test
  ProjectFortress` has no hit).
- **No names added**, so the name greps of the rung protocol (both corpora and
  `src/com/sun/fortress/` whole) have nothing to search for, and the ladder subset is empty: the
  batch record names no ladder file for this rung, no recorded first error names a name of it, and
  the compiled path does not read these files.

## 6. Defects measured, and their homes

- **D1. A declaration's span absorbs the comments that follow it** (new; home 3, because the
  specification is silent). When a declaration ends in an expression or a type, its source span,
  and the unambiguous name the parser derives from the span, run to the end of the comments that
  follow it; one ending in `end` is not affected. `probes/SpanAbsorb.fss` with
  `probes/SpanAbsorb.txt`: `f(x: ZZ32): ZZ32 = x + 1` followed by a line comment spans `4:1~5:63`
  and is named `…SpanAbsorb.fss:4:1-5:63`; the next `f`, followed by a blank line and a block
  comment, spans `6:1~8:41`; `g … end`, followed by a comment, spans `9:1~11:2`; the interpreter's
  dispatch failure lists both `f` with the widened ranges. The parser's `createSpan`
  (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/parser/Fortress.rats:145-157`) steps back from the end of
  the consumed text over space characters only, so a comment consumed at the end of a production
  stays inside the span. Nothing but diagnostics and location-derived names depends on it: in this
  rung it widened three spans and changed no answer (section 5). The specification defines no
  spans; the nearest sentence asks only that "the original source location information" be kept
  across concatenated files (`Specification/basic/components/source-code.tex:37-40`). Row 354,
  provisional, in `record.md`. Not repaired here: the parser is outside a comment-only rung.
- **D2. Row 49 in argument position** (existing row, re-observed; its home stays row 49, with a note).
  An array literal passed straight to an operator is not an array under `walk`:

# Record lines for rung X (`rung-export-var`), for the coordinator to fold at merge time

## FACTS.md

- **A top-level variable imported through an api can be read, assigned and read back on the compiled path (2026-09-20, rung X of climb batch 2).** Mutability was lost twice on the way across the api boundary and both sites are repaired: the checker asked the *component's* type environment whether an api-qualified name was mutable and so refused every such assignment with "Cannot assign to immutable variable" (`scala_src/typechecker/impls/Operators.scala:444`, now routed through the new `isMutableName`, `scala_src/typechecker/STypeChecker.scala:345-350`, written after its four api-aware siblings at `:307,324,334,356`); and `CodeGen.forVarRef`'s fresh-import path built a plain `VarCodeGen.StaticBinding` with the value's descriptor while a mutable variable's singleton field holds R1's `MutableFValue` cell, so the run died with `NoSuchFieldError` (`compiler/codegen/CodeGen.java:5985-5998`, mutability now read from the declaring api's index by `importedVarIsMutable:5960-5967`, the branch `addTopLevelVarBinding:5945-5951` already made for a component's own variables). Gated by `ProjectFortress/compiler_tests/ExportVarRungX.test` with `ExportVarRungXApi.fsi`/`.fss` beside it. `NamingCzar.java` is not touched.
- **An exported function fails exactly as an exported variable does when a component's name differs from the api it exports, and the failure is the repository's, not codegen's (2026-09-20, rung X).** `probes/FnApi.fsi`+`FnLib.fss`+`FnMain.fss` dies with `NoClassDefFoundError: FnApi`, alongside `P8Api$shared` and `P9Api$shared` (`explorations/compile-ladder/rung-export-var/probes/probes-preedit.txt:29,96,163`). Through the real entry points the divergence never reaches codegen at all: `fortress link P8Main` and `walk` on each of the three main components print "Could not find an implementation for API ... on path" (`probes/link-and-walk-preedit.txt:4-9,45-60`), so both execution paths assume the api and its implementing component share a name. The assumption is `Linker.whoIsImplementingMyAPI`'s fallback to the api's own name (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/linker/Linker.java:72-76`) when nothing has been registered in its persisted map, and only the user can register one, by hand, through `LinkShell`'s `alink`/`clink` verbs (`linker/LinkShell.java:41-70`; `linker/README:28-40` describes the intended design). `Specification/basic/components/overview.tex:33-35` settles it -- a reference to an imported api is "resolved to a component that exports that api" -- and the team reserved the codegen half of the repair in three comments in one file (`CodeGen.java:411-441`, `:1856`, `:6599-6606`). Gated as an expected failure by `ProjectFortress/compiler_tests/XXXExportVarRungXLinked.test`.
- **An immutable top-level variable exported through a same-named api already worked before rung X, including at an object type (2026-09-20, rung X).** `probes/SameVarApi.*` prints `fixed = 11` and `probes/ObjVarApi.*`+`ObjVarMain.fss` prints `data.size = 5` with exit 0 on the base tree (`probes/probes-preedit.txt:218`, `probes/link-and-walk-preedit.txt:42-44`). Both microGPT apis export `corpus: Corpus` immutably from an api that shares its component's name (`explorations/apl/mg/MicroGptApl.fsi:18` declares it, `MicroGptApl.fss:12-13` is `component MicroGptApl` exporting `MicroGptApl`; `explorations/run-c4/src/MicroGptFlat.fsi:16` declares it, `MicroGptFlat.fss:9-10` is `component MicroGptFlat` exporting `MicroGptFlat`, and the satisfying declaration is the immutable `corpus: Corpus = loadCorpus(corpusPath, blockSize, bosId)` at `MicroGptFlat.fss:48`), and `MicroGptFlatCheck.fss:38,40,72` is the second component that reads it -- so the shape the two target programs actually use was never blocked, and what rung X adds for them is the mutable case.
- **`ant compileAll` deletes a tracked file (2026-09-20, rung X).** `compileAll` depends on `compileCommon` (`build.xml:539`), which depends on `cleanCache` (`:715`), which deletes `default_repository/caches` entire (`:42,356-359`) -- including the tracked `global.map`, the linker's persisted `RepoState` (`linker/RepoState.java:176`). Every worktree that runs `ant compileAll` therefore shows `D default_repository/caches/global.map` afterwards, and a `git add -A` at that moment commits the deletion; restore it with `git checkout -- default_repository/caches/global.map`.
- **An `XXX*.test` file in `compiler_tests/` cannot carry a `run_out_contains` key (2026-09-20, rung X).** `FileTests.java:583-585` tests `trueFailure != null` before `:587`'s `shouldFail != failed`, so the unmet output assertion fails the test whatever the XXX name says (corrected here by the merged-diff review of 2026-09-20; the version folded into FACTS.md at the gather stage already carries the two line numbers, this staging copy did not); this is one face of the harness author's own warning at `FileTests.java:853`. All 224 existing `XXX*.test` files in that directory assert a diagnostic from a `compile`-family command and none has a `run` line, which is a constraint and not a habit. `XXX0b.test` is the model: it asserts the same "Could not find an implementation for API" diagnostic for a different api.

## Gap ledger

**Row 320** -- append to the notes, do not renumber:

> Repaired in part by rung X of climb batch 2 (2026-09-20), which split the row into two defects and measured that only one of them is the variable's. **Repaired:** mutability is no longer lost when the declaration crosses the api boundary, at both of the two sites that dropped it -- the checker's `env.isMutable(id)` on the importing component's environment (`scala_src/typechecker/impls/Operators.scala:444`, which refused every assignment to an imported mutable variable with "Cannot assign to immutable variable" *before* codegen was ever reached, a third failure mode the row did not name) and `CodeGen.forVarRef`'s always-`StaticBinding` fresh-import path (`compiler/codegen/CodeGen.java:5985-5998`). Gated by `compiler_tests/ExportVarRungX.test`; failure and pass captured in `explorations/compile-ladder/rung-export-var/probes/gated-tests-preedit.txt:15` and `-postedit.txt:9-15`, both at one thread and at four. **Not repaired, and reclassified:** the class-name half is not a variable defect and not a codegen defect. An exported *function* fails identically -- `NoClassDefFoundError: FnApi` from `probes/FnApi.fsi`+`FnLib.fss`+`FnMain.fss`, beside `P8Api$shared` and `P9Api$shared` (`probes/probes-preedit.txt:29,96,163`) -- because `packageAndClassName` is the component's name (`CodeGen.java:390`) while both `functionalRefToPackageClassAndMethod` (`:3761-3818`) and `jvmClassForToplevelDecl` (`NamingCzar.java:1653-1656`) resolve a reference to the api's. Nor is that state reachable through the real entry points: `fortress link P8Main` refuses with "Could not find an implementation for API P8Api on path", and so does the interpreter on all three programs (`probes/link-and-walk-preedit.txt:4-9,45-60`), so the row's `NoClassDefFoundError` is what one gets only by hand-compiling each file with `fortress compile`, which is what the row's original probe did. The assumption that an api and its implementing component share a name belongs to the repository: `Linker.whoIsImplementingMyAPI` returns the api's own name when its persisted map has no entry (`linker/Linker.java:72-76`), and only `LinkShell`'s `alink`/`clink` verbs put entries there (`linker/LinkShell.java:41-70`; the design is in `linker/README:28-40`). `Specification/basic/components/overview.tex:33-35` settles the divergence -- "the references of a component to an imported api are resolved to a component that exports that api" -- and the fix is either a discovery step in `whoIsImplementingMyAPI` or the api-named forwarder the team reserved at `CodeGen.java:411-441`, `:1856` and `:6599-6606`; both are design changes past one rung, which is the stop the batch record named for this rung. That half now has a gated expected-failure test, `compiler_tests/XXXExportVarRungXLinked.test` with `ExportVarRungXLibApi.fsi` and `ExportVarRungXLib.fss` beside it, covering an exported variable and an exported function together; it was shown to go red on a deliberate local fix (`probes/xxx-goes-red.txt`). One further correction to the row's premise: the shape both microGPT apis use -- an *immutable* variable exported from an api that shares its component's name -- already worked before this rung, at `ZZ32` and at an object type (`probes/probes-preedit.txt:218`, `probes/link-and-walk-preedit.txt:42-44`).

**Rows 343 and 344, both rewritten at the gather stage on the skeptic's required
correction 1.** The row this rung first wrote — "the interpreter cannot see a mutable
top-level variable exported through an api at all", NEGATIVE-VERIFIED — was refuted by
`probes/skeptic/skeptic-name-isolation.txt` and is **not** opened. It generalised from one
probe whose variable happened to be called `shared`. What went into the ledger instead, in
manifest order from 343, is the skeptic's pair: 343, the unreported name collision, and
344, the compiler prelude's missing locality functions. Both are folded in full in
`explorations/fortress-gap-ledger.md` (section 10's table) and neither needs restating
here; the two differences from the skeptic's proposed text are that the assignment claim
is now measured (`probes/gather/GatherAssignApi.fsi`+`.fss`+`GatherAssignMain.fss`,
capture `probes/gather/gather-assign.txt`: read 7, assign 23, read back 23, at one thread
and at four), and that row 343's notes correct this rung's report on where its gated home
is: `ProjectFortress/tests/` does honour an `XXX` name — `FileTests.java:711` hands
`s.startsWith("XXX")` to `SourceFileTest` as `shouldFail` and `:384-404` turns such a file
red the day it starts passing, 55 `XXX*.fss` already live there, and
`tests/XXXImportImportCollision.fss` is that corpus's own collision test, importing its
api pair from `ProjectFortress/test_library/`. The reason rung X did not add it is only
that this batch forbids running `ant testSystem`, so it could not be verified before
landing.

**Row 13** (import aliasing) — appended, not renumbered: the skeptic's two-path
measurement of `import SkVarApi.{counter => ctr}`, refused identically by both paths three
times each with "Variable ctr is not defined." (`probes/skeptic/SkAlias.fss`, capture
`probes/skeptic/skeptic-differentials.txt:20-28`, `:104-111`, `:135-143`, `:219-226`).

input.summary:
I added four comments, and no code, to Library/FortressLibrary.fss and .fsi (31 inserted lines, none deleted):
- the closure's NOT YET note, in each file's own form of the team's wording: comprises Integral[\I\] where [\I\];
- why Array3 excludes AnyAdditiveGroup: it chooses one of two uses of rank 3, and Array1 and Array2 cannot carry the exclusion because Vector and Matrix are additive groups;
- that the eight scalar-block operators return the unsized Array[\T,I\];
- that the reversed - means y - e for each element, the block's only operator whose operand order matters.

How it was verified:
- A re-lexer built on Spacing.rats's comment rules shows the diff is comment-only.
- The tree's own parser gives identical trees once positions are remapped, except three span ends.
- The checker-count stage gives 93 errors both before and after, and its whole output is identical line for line after remapping.
- A walk probe of all four declarations prints the same output before and after.
- Four gated interpreter tests that use these declarations pass when run singly.

I did not run the two suites, following the shared prefix. That was a decision against the batch record's 'byte-identical' obligation, and the gate will confirm it after the merge.

I measured one new defect: the parser's createSpan (Fortress.rats:145-157) extends a declaration's span over the comments that follow it. It is recorded as provisional row 354, with a probe (home 3, because the specification is silent). The argument-position form of row 49 was re-observed; a note for that row is in record.md. I did not add an XXX test for it, because that would break this rung's byte-identical-suites obligation.

At launch neither the worktree nor the branch existed. I created both from d610695c0 using the recipe in remote-container.md and pushed the branch before any work.
decisions: I did not run ant testFast or testSystem in the worktree. I followed the shared prefix's ban rather than the batch record's 'both suites byte-identical' obligation, and replaced the suites with cheaper evidence: a re-lexing check, a parse-tree comparison, the checker-count stage and walk probes. The alternative was to run both suites before and after, here.

Each file keeps its own comment form: the .fss form '(** \vspace{-4ex} NOT YET: %...% *)' and the .fsi form '(** not yet: ``%...%'' *)'. The alternative was the brief's quoted .fss form in both files.

The honest clause is spelled 'comprises Integral[\I\] where [\I\]' without braces, as the team spells its single-type notes. The alternatives were the brief's braced form, or spelling out the bound as the HasRank note does.
The closure note goes on the line after the one-line trait. The alternative, inside the trait body as the precedents are, would have changed a code line.
The .fsi scalar block gets the .fss block's header line, so that 'All eight' has a referent. The alternative was a self-contained first sentence.
The example is written in Fortress array syntax, '3 - [1 2] is [2 1]'. The alternative was the brief's '[1, 2]'.

I added no XXX test for row 49's argument-position form, because it would break the byte-identical obligation and the declared testSystem count of 385. The alternative was an XXX file in ProjectFortress/tests/ and an undeclared 386.

I kept the comments beside the reversed - and in the .fsi even though, because of D1, they widen three spans. The alternatives were to leave the .fsi uncommented or to move the note away from the reversed -, both against the brief.
I created the missing worktree and branch myself from d610695c0 using remote-container.md:96-110, rather than stopping.
defectHomes: D1, new: the span of a declaration that ends in an expression or a type runs over the comments after it, and so does its location-derived unambiguous name (createSpan, Fortress.rats:145-157). Home 3, because the specification defines no spans (source-code.tex:37-40 is the nearest sentence). Probe: explorations/compile-ladder/rung-library-comments/probes/SpanAbsorb.fss with SpanAbsorb.txt. Ledger row 354 (provisional) is in record.md.

D2, re-observed, existing row 49: an untyped array literal in argument position is an IUOTuple, not an array (Evaluator.java:725-732), so '3 - [1 2]' fails dispatch. Its home stays row 49, and record.md holds a note to append to it (probes/ArrayLiteralArg.fss with ArrayLiteralArg.txt). The specification settles it (aggregate.tex:129-137), but I added no XXX test because this rung must keep the suites byte-identical (decision in REPORT.md section 9).

Not code defects: the brief and the explainer cite the reversed - at .fss:4501, but at the base it was at :4500. Separately, this rung makes the assert message at ProjectFortress/library_tests/TryAtomicRungB.fss:42 stale: its '.fss:1570' should now read ':1571'. That is flagged for the coordinator in record.md, because the fix is not a comment.
divergences: walk and the compiled run were not compared: the compiled path does not import FortressLibrary. The one related two-sided observation is row 49's argument-position form, walk against the specification: aggregate.tex:129-137 gives an array literal an Array type in every context, so the specification favours the language's meaning over walk.
notDone: ant testFast and ant testSystem were not run, per the shared prefix. The byte-identical counts and summaries are for the post-merge gate to confirm.
No XXX test for row 49's argument-position form: it belongs in ProjectFortress/tests/ in a rung whose manifest declares the count.
Row 354 is not repaired: the parser is outside a comment-only rung.
The TryAtomicRungB.fss:42 citation (:1570 should now be :1571) is left for the coordinator.

I did not measure whether the compile-path checker accepts a user Matrix-by-Array3 operator. Comment 2's claim that it causes no overloading collision rests on the specification (overloading.tex:178-216) and the explainer.
